answer.rationale: A release went out 2 hours ago; write-path latency began climbing 90 minutes ago—tight temporal coupling. memory_b1 documents a prior identical pattern where rollback cleared the checkout error spike quickly and safely. memory_b6 shows we've successfully staged releases so that any bad build has already had canary confirmation. Rollback is the lowest-latency, highest-confidence intervention: it preserves settlement writes in place, avoids redistributing load during peak (regional_failover), avoids provisioning delay (add_capacity), avoids masking a real defect (enable_circuit_breaker), and avoids shifting load that may already be saturated on a write path (route_read_replicas).
